name: P.V. Krishna Reddy
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2010-2025); Hurun Global (2018); Hurun India (2016)
forbes_bio: P.V. Krishna Reddy is the managing director of privately held Megha Engineering and Infrastructure.
He cofounded it with his uncle, P.P. Reddy, in 1989 to build small pipes for municipalities.
Megha soon expanded into building infrastructure projects such as dams, natural gas distribution networks, power plants and roads.
Megha also has projects overseas in Zambia, Tanzania, Bangladesh and Kuwait.

name: James Leininger
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2012-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: James Leininger, known as "Doctor Jim," made his fortune founding medical devices company Kinetic Concepts (KCI), which focuses on wound care.
In 2012, private equity firm Apax Partners led a $6.3 billion acquisition of the company. Leininger was the largest shareholder.
He also founded the Texas Public Policy Foundation in 1989 to support free-market policies and research.
He has mostly invested through his Medcare Investment Funds, which manages $1 billion in assets.
forbes_facts: Leininger started KCI in an one-bedroom apartment in 1976.
Leininger has a small stake in NBA's San Antonio Spurs.

name: Anne Marie See Pastor
forbes_bio: See Pastor is the daughter of Carlos Rodriguez-Pastor, a Peruvian politician who along with outside investors acquired Banco Internacional del Peru in 1994.
Her billionaire brother, Carlos, took over leadership of the bank after his father died and has since  invested its profits in other businesses.
A political coup sent the family exile in California in the 1980s; when they returned, the elder Rodriguez-Pastor served as Minister of Economy from 1982 to 1984.
The family owns the majority of the publicly traded company Intercorp Financial Services.

name: Greg Brown
sec_insider_companies: Motorola Solutions, Inc. (MSI) - Chairman and CEO
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Hurun Global (2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Greg Brown has been CEO of Motorola Solutions since 2008 and chairman since 2011.
He is the longest-serving chief executive of the company formerly known as Motorola, Inc. after the firm's cofounder Paul Galvin (d. 1959) and his son Bob Galvin (d. 2011).
Brown spun off Motorola's struggling legacy smartphone business in 2011, and the Razr maker was acquired by Google for $12.5 billion a year later. (It's now part of Lenovo.)

Through more than 50 acquisitions, Brown has transformed Motorola Solutions into a $10.8 billion (2024 revenue) behemoth in the market for mission-critical public safety communications, 911 command center solutions and video security.
Brown has netted more than $700 million (before taxes) exercising options and selling shares of Motorola Solutions. He owns 1% of the company between his remaining stock and options.

name: Philip Green
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2004-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2024); Wikidata (2016)
forbes_bio: Philip Green and his wife Cristina Green once sat atop the British retail empire Arcadia Group.
The business was forced to sell its best-known brands ? including Topshop, Top Man and Dorothy Perkins ? after it fell into bankruptcy in 2020.
The Greens have been vilified in Britain for their role in letting home retailer BHS collapse, which put pensions for 19,000 workers at risk in 2016.
Parliament voted to strip Green of his knighthood over the pension deficit scandal. However, he is still a knight; the vote was symbolic.

forbes_facts: A college dropout, Philip Green started his first business at age 21, importing jeans from Asia with a $30,000 loan from his family.

name: Nie Tengyun
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2017-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026); Hurun China (2016-2026)
forbes_bio: Nie Tengyun is the chairman and president of Yunda Holding, one of China's largest express delivery companies.
The company finished a backdoor listing in China in December 2016 and changed the listed company's name from Ningbo Xinhai Electric to Yunda Holding.
Nie established the company in 1999 with only 17 employees; today, it employs more than 9,000 people.

name: Michael Kum
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Hotel tycoon Michael Kum runs a hospitality empire spanning 21 hotels across Asia and Europe through his privately held M&L Hospitality.
Daughter Jocelyn Kum, who was an executive director on the board of M & L Hospitality, took over as CEO of M & L Hospitality in May 2026.
The son of street hawkers, Kum got into hotels in 2009 after selling his offshore barges business to Macquarie Group.
In June 2025, he acquired Hotel Maria, a 116-room luxury hotel in Helsinki, Finland. It will be rebranded as Waldorf Astoria Helsinki and managed by Hilton.
Family also has investments in Singapore-based organic grocer Little Farms; U.K.-based AI-driven pest detection company Spotta and Australia-based food waste management outfit Goterra.
forbes_facts: He cofounded Offshore Equipment in 1976, chartering vessels and barges to the oil and gas industry.
He also has a stake in Australian vessel operator, MMA Offshore.

name: Grigory Anikeev
forbes_bio: Grigory Anikeev owns ABI Group, a Russian conglomerate with interests in food, retail and real estate.
ABI Product, the largest division of ABI Group, is the largest Russian producer of sausage products and frozen food with revenue of about $1 billion.
Anikeev has been deputy of The State Duma, the lower house of the Russian parliament, since 2007, and is a member of President Vladimir Putin's United Russia Party.
In 2020, Anikeev declared the highest annual income among State Duma deputies - 2.7 billion rubles ($38 million).
forbes_facts: ABI Group is an acronym for Anikeev Business Invest.
